# TerminusDB

> TerminusDB is the open-source knowledge graph database with git-like version control for graphs and vectors. Branch, merge, diff and hybrid search any commit.

TerminusDB stores JSON documents as a typed graph with a schema. Every write is an immutable commit, so you can branch, diff, merge, push, pull, clone and query any earlier commit. You query with WOQL (a Datalog), with GraphQL, or with the HTTP Documents API. The server listens on `http://localhost:6363`. Source: https://github.com/terminusdb/terminusdb (Apache 2.0).

Notes for agents:

- Load [llms-full.txt](https://terminusdb.com/llms-full.txt) (all docs pages in one file) when you write non-trivial WOQL, build document schemas, use the version-control API (clone/push/pull/rebase), configure TerminusDB Enterprise document formats (Turtle, RDF/XML, JSON-LD), work with VectorLink search, or write date, time, duration or interval queries (`xdd:dateTimeInterval`, Allen's relations).
- For exact WOQL predicate names, argument order and argument types, start from the [WOQL class reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-class-reference-guide/). It is generated from the WOQL schema, so it lists every predicate.
- When a query, insert or schema change fails, see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) below before you guess.
- Every docs page is also served as raw Markdown at `<page-url>/page.md`, for example `https://terminusdb.com/docs/glossary/page.md`.

## Get started

- [Get started in 10 minutes](https://terminusdb.com/docs/get-started/): run TerminusDB with Docker, clone a sample dataset, then branch, diff and merge it. Includes a paste-in prompt to set it up with an AI coding agent.
- [Clone a demo dataset](https://terminusdb.com/docs/clone-a-demo-project/): start from Star Wars or Ecommerce data.
- [Documentation home](https://terminusdb.com/docs/start-here/): pick a quickstart by language and role.
- [What is TerminusDB?](https://terminusdb.com/docs/terminusdb-explanation/): how it works and who it is for.

```bash
docker run --pull always -d -p 127.0.0.1:6363:6363 \
  -v terminusdb_storage:/app/terminusdb/storage \
  --name terminusdb terminusdb/terminusdb-server:v12
```

Default credentials for local development: user `admin`, password `root`.

## Schema

- [Schema reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/schema-reference-guide/): the most important page for building on TerminusDB. Classes, properties, subdocuments, key strategies, enums and type rules.
- [Document model](https://terminusdb.com/docs/documents-explanation/): documents, subdocuments and graph relationships.
- [Schema CRUD operations](https://terminusdb.com/docs/schema-crud-operations/): create, read, update and delete classes with the Document API and `graph_type=schema`.
- [Prefix management](https://terminusdb.com/docs/prefix-management/): the `@context` object, `@base` (document IRIs) and `@schema` (class and property IRIs).
- [XSD data types](https://terminusdb.com/docs/xsd-data-types/): the `xsd:` types you can use for fields.
- [Schema migration reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/schema-migration-reference-guide/): add fields, rename properties, change types and re-key documents.
- [Troubleshooting the data model](https://terminusdb.com/docs/troubleshooting-data-model/): wrong `@id` format, Set vs Array, Optional fields and `@key` problems.

Key strategies (`@key`): `Lexical` (IRI from the `@fields` values), `Hash` (SHA-256 of the `@fields` values), `ValueHash` (hash of the whole document), `Random`, `UuidV7` (time-ordered UUID, accepts any supplied `@id`). A `@subdocument` class must use `Random`, `UuidV7` or `ValueHash`.

A minimal schema: a plain field, an `Optional` field, a `Set` of links, and a subdocument. Post it to the schema graph:

```bash
curl -u admin:root -X POST \
  "http://localhost:6363/api/document/admin/MyDatabase?graph_type=schema&author=admin&message=Add+classes" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '[
    {"@type": "Class", "@id": "Person",
     "@key": {"@type": "Lexical", "@fields": ["name"]},
     "name": "xsd:string",
     "nickname": {"@type": "Optional", "@class": "xsd:string"},
     "friends": {"@type": "Set", "@class": "Person"},
     "address": "Address"},
    {"@type": "Class", "@id": "Address",
     "@key": {"@type": "Random"},
     "@subdocument": [],
     "street": "xsd:string",
     "country": "xsd:string"}
  ]'
```

## Documents API

- [HTTP Documents API](https://terminusdb.com/docs/http-documents-api/): create, read, update and delete schema and documents over REST, no client needed.
- [Document API reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/document-insertion/): all parameters for the document endpoint.
- [OpenAPI reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/openapi/): every HTTP endpoint.

```bash
curl -u admin:root -X POST \
  "http://localhost:6363/api/document/admin/MyDatabase/local/branch/main?author=admin&message=Add+document&raw_json=true" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"@type": "Person", "@id": "terminusdb:///data/jane", "name": "Jane Smith", "age": 30}'
```

## Migrate from MongoDB

- [Migrate from MongoDB](https://terminusdb.com/docs/migrate-from-mongodb/): full guide — licensing, verbatim raw JSON, prefix collections, WOQL and path queries, gradual schema contracts, and the missing mechanisms to plan for.

The migration path in one paragraph: TerminusDB is Apache 2.0 (MongoDB's SSPLv1 is not OSI-approved and copylefts hosted-service stacks); `raw_json=true` inserts store `sys:JSONDocument`s that read back semantically verbatim since 12.1 — content `@id`/`@type` members are data, `raw_id=false` is the default, `identifiers=false` no longer strips raw content. A MongoDB collection maps to an IRI prefix: name documents `orders/<key>` and `id_prefix=orders/` lists them via a sorted-dictionary range seek (`format=ids`, `counted=true`). Query with WOQL over `/api/woql` (Datalog: triple patterns, `group_by`, `order_by`, `path`). Raw JSON structure navigates with `json:`-predicated path hops, but `{"@id"}` members store the IRI as a string — first-class document-to-document link traversal needs schema'd class fields, which is the gradual-contracts path: schemaless (`schema_check:false`) → declared classes → linked traversable graphs. Missing for MongoDB users (issue candidates): field-level updates, aggregation-pipeline stages, `$text` search, TTL/capped collections, per-document change streams, listing sort/projection, geospatial, mixed bulk writes.

```bash
# Insert + verbatim read of a raw JSON document named under a prefix
curl -u admin:root -X POST \
  "http://localhost:6363/api/document/admin/shop/local/branch/main?author=you&message=order&raw_json=true" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"@id": "orders/2024-001", "customer": "Alice", "total": 19.98}'
curl -u admin:root \
  "http://localhost:6363/api/document/admin/shop/local/branch/main?id_prefix=orders/&as_list=true"
```

## WOQL

- [WOQL basics](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-basics/): pattern matching and graph traversal with the Datalog query language.
- [WOQL overview](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-explanation/): how WOQL works. Available in the JS and Python clients and as JSON over `/api/woql`.
- [Learn WOQL](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-tutorial/): interactive tutorial with runnable examples.
- [WOQL how-to](https://terminusdb.com/docs/how-to-query-with-woql/): common query tasks.
- [Path queries](https://terminusdb.com/docs/path-queries-in-woql/): follow chains of relationships across the graph.
- [WOQL class reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-class-reference-guide/): every WOQL predicate with its exact arguments. Check names here.
- [WOQL as raw JSON-LD](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-json-ld-queries/): the wire format (`Triple`, `NodeValue`, `DataValue`, `And`). Post WOQL over HTTP without a client.
- [Run a WOQL query](https://terminusdb.com/docs/run-woql-query/): over HTTP, TypeScript or Python.
- [Common WOQL patterns](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-common-patterns/): filter, join, aggregate, path, insert, update, delete and time-travel queries to adapt.
- [WOQL data handling](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-data-handling/): data types, variable binding, typecasting, dicts, lists, `group_by`, CSV and JSON.
- [WOQL control flow](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-control-flow/): backtracking, variable scope across sub-queries, and query performance.
- [Path query reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/path-query-reference-guide/): the full path pattern grammar.
- [What is unification?](https://terminusdb.com/docs/what-is-unification/): how WOQL variables bind.
- [Query cookbook](https://terminusdb.com/docs/terminusdb-query-cookbook/): recipes for WOQL and GraphQL.
- [WOQL tips and tricks](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-tips-and-tricks-1/): optional bindings, debugging and query composition.
- [Numeric precision](https://terminusdb.com/docs/numeric-precision-reference/): exact `xsd:decimal` arithmetic versus IEEE 754 `xsd:double` and `xsd:float`.

```javascript
// triple: subject, predicate, object — 'v:name' declares a variable
WOQL.triple('v:person', 'name', 'v:name')
// read a document by id
WOQL.read_document('Person/Jane', 'v:doc')
```

The same kind of query as raw JSON-LD over HTTP (from [Run a WOQL query](https://terminusdb.com/docs/run-woql-query/)). It returns every triple, with variables `Subject`, `Predicate` and `Object`:

```bash
curl -u admin:root -X POST http://localhost:6363/api/woql/admin/MyDatabase/local/branch/main \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query": {"@type": "Triple", "subject": {"@type": "NodeValue", "variable": "Subject"}, "predicate": {"@type": "NodeValue", "variable": "Predicate"}, "object": {"@type": "Value", "variable": "Object"}}}'
```

Common pitfalls (stale training data):

- Do not use string concatenation in queries. Use WOQL variables (`v:name`) and unification.
- Pick the numeric type on purpose. `xsd:decimal` and `xsd:integer` are stored as rationals and their arithmetic is exact (`0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3`; decimals are capped at 20 digits). `xsd:double` and `xsd:float` are IEEE 754 floats, and if any operand is a float the result is `xsd:double`.
- The `path()` operator takes a pattern over field names: `A,B` sequence, `A|B` choice, `F+`, `F*`, `F{n,m}`, `.` any field, `(A)` group, `F>` forward (same as `F`) and `<F` backward. Example: `path('v:a', '(<pilot,pilot>)+', 'v:b')` goes back along `pilot` to a vehicle, then forward to another pilot, one or more times.
- Document IDs are IRIs such as `'Person/Jane'`, not bare strings or numeric keys.
- In raw JSON-LD WOQL, a variable is `{"@type": "NodeValue", "variable": "Person"}`, without the `v:` prefix, and the key is `variable`, not `var`.

## Time, dates and intervals

TerminusDB has ISO 8601 time types and WOQL predicates for comparison, ranges, sequences, durations and Allen's interval algebra. They shipped in [TerminusDB 12.0.4](https://terminusdb.com/docs/releases/12-0-4-range-queries-time-intervals/).

- [WOQL time handling](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-time-handling/): ISO 8601 types, comparators (`gte`, `lte`, `in_range`), `sequence`, durations and the "inclusive in, half-open inside" pattern.
- [Allen's interval algebra](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-interval-algebra/): the `xdd:dateTimeInterval` type, inclusive versus half-open intervals, `interval_relation` and `interval_relation_typed`, and worked examples of all 13 Allen relations.
- [dateTimeInterval semantics](https://terminusdb.com/docs/datetime-interval-semantics/): how plain date endpoints are stored as UTC datetimes.
- [End-of-month rules](https://terminusdb.com/docs/woql-eom-rules/): month-based duration arithmetic that keeps month-end dates on month-end.
- [Time processing tutorials](https://terminusdb.com/docs/time-processing/): four tutorials, from [dates](https://terminusdb.com/docs/time-tutorial-dates/) and [durations](https://terminusdb.com/docs/time-tutorial-durations/) to [intervals](https://terminusdb.com/docs/time-tutorial-intervals/) and [temporal patterns](https://terminusdb.com/docs/time-tutorial-patterns/).

Intervals are half-open: the start is included and the end is not. `interval_relation(Rel, XStart, XEnd, YStart, YEnd)` checks one of the 13 relations (`before`, `after`, `meets`, `met_by`, `overlaps`, `overlapped_by`, `starts`, `started_by`, `during`, `contains`, `finishes`, `finished_by`, `equals`). Leave `Rel` as a variable to find which relation holds.

```javascript
// Q1 [Jan 1, Apr 1) meets Q2 [Apr 1, Jul 1): no gap, no overlap
WOQL.interval_relation("meets",
  literal("2025-01-01", "xsd:date"), literal("2025-04-01", "xsd:date"),
  literal("2025-04-01", "xsd:date"), literal("2025-07-01", "xsd:date"))
// Succeeds
```

For two `xdd:dateTimeInterval` values, use `interval_relation_typed(Rel, X, Y)`.

## GraphQL

- [GraphQL basics](https://terminusdb.com/docs/graphql-basics/): every database gets a GraphQL schema and endpoint at `/api/graphql/<org>/<db>`.
- [Query with GraphQL](https://terminusdb.com/docs/how-to-query-with-graphql/): filter, order and page through documents.
- [GraphQL query reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/graphql-query-reference/): all query arguments and back links.
- [GraphQL mutations](https://terminusdb.com/docs/graphql-mutations/): write documents with GraphQL.

## Clients

- [JavaScript/TypeScript client](https://terminusdb.com/docs/use-the-javascript-client/) (official): `npm install terminusdb`. [Quickstart](https://terminusdb.com/docs/connect-with-the-javascript-client/).
- [Python client](https://terminusdb.com/docs/use-the-python-client/) (official): `pip install terminusdb-client`. [Quickstart](https://terminusdb.com/docs/connect-with-python-client/).
- [Rust client](https://terminusdb.com/docs/rust-client-quickstart/) (community): `cargo add terminusdb-client`.
- [Elixir client](https://hex.pm/packages/terminusdb_client) (community): the `terminusdb_client` package on Hex.

```javascript
import TerminusClient from 'terminusdb'
const client = new TerminusClient.WOQLClient('http://localhost:6363', {
  user: 'admin', organization: 'admin', key: 'root',
})
await client.createDatabase('MyDatabase')
```

```python
from terminusdb_client import Client
client = Client("http://localhost:6363")
client.connect(team="admin", key="root")
client.create_database("MyDatabase")
```

## Vector and hybrid search

- [Versioned Search](https://terminusdb.com/docs/versioned-search/): VectorLink semantic, full-text and hybrid search, with one snapshot per commit. TerminusDB 12.1 release candidate.
- [Versioned Search quickstart](https://terminusdb.com/docs/versioned-search-quickstart/): start the stack, index a commit and search. The default embedding model runs locally on CPU, no API key.
- [Push indexing](https://terminusdb.com/docs/versioned-search-indexing/): TerminusDB builds the text to embed from your schema and pushes each commit to VectorLink automatically.
- [Search concepts](https://terminusdb.com/docs/versioned-search-concepts/): domains, commits, chunks, search modes and embedding providers.
- [Embedded engine](https://terminusdb.com/docs/versioned-search-embedded/): run VectorLink inside the TerminusDB process.

## Versioning

- [Version control operations](https://terminusdb.com/docs/version-control-operations/): branch, commit, diff, merge, squash and reset, with HTTP examples.
- [Merge branches](https://terminusdb.com/docs/merge-howto/): apply changes, find conflicts and resolve them.
- [JSON diff and patch](https://terminusdb.com/docs/json-diff-and-patch/): the engine behind version control. Compute and apply structural diffs between documents or commits.
- [Time travel queries](https://terminusdb.com/docs/time-travel-howto/): read commit history and query the data at any earlier commit.
- [Git-for-data reference](https://terminusdb.com/docs/git-for-data-reference/): push, pull, fetch, clone, rebase and remotes.
- [Clone a database](https://terminusdb.com/docs/clone/), [push](https://terminusdb.com/docs/push-to-project/) and [pull](https://terminusdb.com/docs/pull-from-project/): sync commits with a remote database.

```bash
# create a branch
curl -u admin:root -X POST http://localhost:6363/api/branch/admin/MyDatabase/local/branch/feature \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"origin": "admin/MyDatabase/local/branch/main"}'
```

## Install

- [Install with Docker Compose](https://terminusdb.com/docs/install-terminusdb-as-a-docker-container/): the `docker-compose.yml` in the main repo starts TerminusDB on port 6363.
- [Snap package](https://snapcraft.io/terminusdb): TerminusDB on the command line, as a git-for-data client and server for push and pull.
- [Installation options](https://terminusdb.com/docs/terminusdb-install-options/): Docker, Kubernetes and source.
- [Kubernetes](https://terminusdb.com/docs/install-on-kubernetes/): run TerminusDB on a cluster.
- [Self-hosted in production](https://terminusdb.com/docs/self-hosted-installation/): production configuration for Docker, Compose and bare metal.
- [TerminusDB Cloud](https://terminusdb.com/docs/cloud/): hosting options.

## Troubleshooting

- [Troubleshooting queries](https://terminusdb.com/docs/troubleshooting-queries/): anyURI vs string mismatches, unbound variables, empty results and path query syntax.
- [Troubleshooting schemas](https://terminusdb.com/docs/troubleshooting-schema/): type mismatches on insert, missing required fields, class not found and enum errors.
- [Troubleshooting the data model](https://terminusdb.com/docs/troubleshooting-data-model/): `@id` format, Set vs Array, Optional and `@key` problems.
- [Your first 15 minutes](https://terminusdb.com/docs/first-15-minutes/): a known-good curl walkthrough to check your setup.
